summary: Observed increasing DB pool latency, pool exhaustion, and high query counts per bulk request leading to HTTP timeouts and degraded healthcheck queue depth; occasional network retransmissions noted but not directly linked.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:10:30Z ERROR [order-service] [db-pool] Pool exhausted: 20/20 active connections held by bulk order serializer
evidence.interpretation: DB connection pool reached its maximum capacity, all 20 connections in use, indicating strong pool pressure during bulk order processing.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:10:05Z ERROR [order-service] [http-worker-4] GET /api/v1/orders/bulk?page=3 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT - 10002ms (queries executed: 184 before timeout)
evidence.interpretation: HTTP request for bulk orders timed out after >10 s after executing many queries, reflecting request‑level latency issues.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:15:00Z ERROR [order-service] [http-worker-1] Healthcheck degraded: DB query queue depth = 142
evidence.interpretation: Healthcheck reports a large DB query queue depth, suggesting backlog in query processing.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:09:12Z WARN [order-service] [db-pool] Query pool latency exceeding threshold: 450ms avg wait
evidence.interpretation: Average wait time for acquiring a DB connection rose above the acceptable threshold, indicating growing contention.
Bulk order request completed successfully but took 890 ms and issued 250 queries, showing high per‑request query volume.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:12:15Z ERROR [order-service] [http-worker-2] GET /api/v1/orders/1002 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR - TimeoutAcquiringConnection: pool empty
evidence.interpretation: Request failed due to inability to acquire a DB connection, reinforcing evidence of pool exhaustion.

evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-28T14:11:00Z WARN [order-service] [network-monitor] TCP retransmissions observed on replica bond0 (packet_loss=0.01%) - distractor
evidence.interpretation: Minor network retransmissions observed; low packet loss suggests limited impact on the primary symptoms.
